openings.claim: Use the right-contact card as a diagnostic perturbation of removable padded jaws with independent bolt-shank edge stops. Geometry and capacity remain unknown.
openings.delta: Change lateral restraint from seal friction to edge contact through strips into the rim. Allocate four strips as two jaw pairs, four bolts as fasteners and two as stops, only if feasible. Card input travels through rim, seal and hatch into rocking and jaw unloading. Treat visible tilt as a veto on extra tightening and inspect stop engagement; nearest rival is friction-dominated retention.
openings.prediction: At nominally unchanged jaw settings, engaged stops should limit sideways movement despite card-induced rocking better than withdrawn stops. The rival predicts restraint follows jaw/seal contact loss. Stable position in both configurations leaves the rival unresolved. No tilt may mean pad compliance or ineffective perturbation; jaw migration or changed preload can cancel attribution. Tilt alone proves neither load path.
openings.probe: Preflight accessible rim, bolt reach, independent stop withdrawal, recoverable cord attachment and clearance of the entire opening after release. Drill/cut strips only. Establish fabrication and observation capacity before testing. Mark jaw settings and hatch position. Run two withdrawn-stop closure/pull trials, one disturbed, then ten engaged-stop opening cycles and closure/pull trials, disturbing the final closure. For each disturbed closure insert the supplied right-contact card; record corner lift and whether stops remain engaged before applying 20 N. Do not compensate by tightening. Record movement, reopening time and seal condition each cycle. Twelve trials cover two configurations, both disturbed. Stop before deformation or further tearing; report incomplete evidence if time expires.
assumptions: Rim geometry and supplied bolts permit this allocation and survive rocking without stop disengagement.
Pads and nominal setting marks do not establish equal preload; ruler resolution limits interpretation.

assessment: Probe, not deployment. Slip above 1 mm, failure at 20 N, reopening above thirty seconds, new tears or obstructed opening defeats acceptance. Resource/capacity failure defeats feasibility. Only disturbed seal continuity is waived.

lineage.reason: Make disturbance a load-path diagnostic with explicit cancelling signals.
Keep twelve-trial allocation; add perturbation path, response and attribution limits.
